protocol.name: cupertino_scroll_v1

description.summary: the scroll count of a pointer

protocol.description: wl_pointer carries the distance of a scroll but not its scroll count: the number of consecutive flicks of one scrolling gesture series, which first-party applications use to scroll further for repeated flicks. This protocol delivers it next to the pointer's axis events. The protocol is unstable until phase 1 of ends: interfaces may change without a version bump until then.

interface.name: cupertino_scroll_v1

description.summary: scroll count services of the server

interface.description: Global singleton. Any client may bind it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created through this global stay valid.

request.name: get_scroll

description.summary: follow the scroll count of a pointer

request.description: Creates an object that tells the client the scroll count of the scrolls the server sends to that wl_pointer. A pointer may have several of them.

interface.name: cupertino_pointer_scroll_v1

description.summary: the scroll count of a wl_pointer

interface.description: The server counts per scroll gesture series of a touchpad and sends the count of the current series for every axis that the next wl_pointer.frame carries a non-stop wl_pointer.axis for. Scrolls of a wheel have no count and no event: a client reads the absence as a count of 0.

event.name: scroll_count

description.summary: the scroll count of the scroll in this frame

event.description: Sent after the wl_pointer.axis event of the axis and before the wl_pointer.frame that ends the group. The count is 0 while no series has started (a scroll too slow to start one), 1 for the first flick, 2 for a second flick that follows within the time between gestures, and from the third on it grows with the speed of the scroll, up to 2000.
